prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of policy proposals (2005), excluding ideological framing:

Economy and taxation:
- Introduce more progressive income tax bands (e.g., 50% over £50,000; 60% over £100,000).
- Add corporation tax bands, with 40% on profits above £1.5m; encourage smaller businesses.
- Increase taxes on unearned wealth; reform inheritance tax so it is paid by recipients and is progressively banded.
- Abolish National Insurance and raise equivalent revenue via income taxation on earned and unearned income; remove employers’ NIC.
- Pilot a Land Value Tax set by local authorities to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Phase out VAT and replace it with revenue-neutral eco-taxes linked to resource use, pollution and waste (e.g., aviation fuel, plastic bags).
- Promote economic localisation: support community banks, credit unions, micro-credit, local currencies; support SMEs and co-ops; oppose entry to the euro; pursue WTO reform.
- Uphold workers’ rights, union representation, and the right to strike; reduce working hours (see Welfare).
- Develop alternative wellbeing metrics to GDP (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate:
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence with targets: -20% CO2 by 2010, -50% by 2020, -85% by 2030; expand carbon trading.
- Replace domestic VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; protect low users via tariff design and no standing charges.
- Reach 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; shift R&D/subsidies from nuclear to renewables; deploy 2m m² solar and 2m small wind systems by 2010; expand on/offshore wind, wave, and biogas.
- Reduce demand: Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy use 30% in 10 years; Smart Energy Councils target 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- Decommission nuclear power stations at end of life; end nuclear R&D subsidies.
- Create a Cabinet post to coordinate climate policy.

Welfare, housing, families:
- Phase in a universal, non-means-tested Citizen’s Income replacing most benefits/tax credits; retain and add specialist benefits (e.g., disability); initially keep Housing Benefit.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension at the Pension Credit Guarantee level, indexed to earnings; abolish Pension Credit means test.
- Simplify child support by enhancing universal benefits; initial step could raise child benefit by ~35%.
- End the Working Time Directive opt-out; review for a 35-hour average week; expand Sure Start.
- Increase affordable housing: allow councils to reinvest sale receipts, support self-build co-ops, apply LVT, and fund insulation/efficiency upgrades.

Health and education:
- Restore a universal, comprehensive NHS; end reliance on PPPs; oppose service marketisation.
- Abolish prescription charges; reinstate free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Raise health funding to ~9% of GNP (~£90bn by 2008); hypothecate an NHS Tax; long-term shifts from defence savings.
- Increase education funding, especially pre-school and post-16; abolish SATs; replace with Individual Learning Plans.
- Scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; later integrate support into the Citizen’s Income.

Transport:
- Target a 10% road-traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road building to public transport.
- Re-regulate buses; integrate tickets and networks; prioritise walking/cycling and mixed-use planning; curb school-run traffic.
- Return rail and tube (track and operations) to public ownership as franchises expire; expand rail lines, freight, stations, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs: expand congestion charging/road pricing; increase fuel duty; abolish car tax disc; set freight duty by size/axle/pollution; support R&D in efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: resist airport expansion; ban night flights; seek EU aviation fuel tax; levy domestic flight emissions tax; raise Air Passenger Duty.

Environment, food, farming:
- Zero Waste Strategy: legislate to cut packaging, outlaw incineration, set recycled-content standards; create a Zero Waste Agency; aim for 60% household recycling by 2010.
- Establish an Environmental Protection Commission; levy eco-taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen EU chemicals rules; promote biodegradable substitutes.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, and nanotech; oppose patents on genetic/natural resources (TRIPS reform).
- Animal welfare: end live exports; ban battery eggs (incl. enriched); seek stronger EU broiler rules; ban fur imports; phase out blood sports and animal testing, replacing with humane methods.
- Set an Organics Target of 30% by 2012; replace the CAP/CFP with support for organic, local markets and biodiversity.
- Ban GM food; toughen and enforce a legally binding supermarkets’ Code of Practice; enhance OFT scrutiny of convenience store acquisitions.

Crime and justice:
- Emphasise prevention: safer urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more caretakers/attendants; address drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards.
- Expand community policing, local stations, and neighbourhood committees; reintroduce park keepers and bus conductors.
- Tighten gun control: quantitative lethality threshold (0.5 joules), prohibit specified weapon types, regulate deactivated arms, unified licensing with competence and stability checks; create a Gun Safety Advisory Committee.
- Scale up restorative justice; improve detection of hate crimes; national strategy on violence against women; support an EU Disability Directive.

Democracy and constitutional reform:
- Oppose national ID cards and a central biometric database.
- Devolve power: strengthen local councils, allow LVT-based local taxation, adopt proportional representation (PR) for local and Westminster elections, enable recall (40%) and local referenda (20% trigger).
- Democratise English regional governance and enhance devolved powers in Scotland/Wales subject to public support.
- Replace the House of Lords with a fully elected PR chamber.
- Draft a written constitution; disestablish the national church; remove formal state roles from the monarchy.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while supporting institutional reform to improve transparency and democracy.

International policy:
- Withdraw troops from Iraq and support UN peacekeeping.
- Reduce defence spending to the EU average; end subsidies/credits for arms exports; close export-promotion bodies; pursue an Arms Trade Treaty; decommission nuclear weapons; renounce CBR/DU use.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax; enable North–South carbon credit transfers.
- Reform the UN Security Council (end permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank with poverty-prevention and sustainability mandates.
- Reform global trade: replace or amend WTO rules via a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade to enable localisation and higher social/environmental standards.
- Asylum and migration: resource faster decisions; allow work and benefits access; independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; uphold the 1951 Refugee Convention; review national laws on legal access, childcare, and subsistence; support improved EU-wide standards.
